learning_outcomes.text: Students can phenomenologically describe the structure of fixed-wing aircraft and the basics of their aerodynamics.
Calculate the flow processes on airfoils and the forces occurring there.
Describe the basics of aerospace measurement technology and electronic flight control, as well as the structure and functionality of aerospace actuators and sensors.
Partly calculate or systematically analyze aerospace actuators and sensors.
Assess the applicability of the mentioned topics in automatic flight control.

syllabus_topics: Stall and measures for improving stall characteristics
Functional principles and basic structure of cockpit systems
Aircraft sensors (aerodynamic, inertial, laser, radar, and satellite-based)
Designing and manufacturing measuring devices or actuators in practical exercises

assessment_methods.method: Examination (written exam, oral exam, or presentation) for MABB441A (Aerodynamics)
Examination (written exam, oral exam, or presentation) for MABB442A (Flight Instruments)

assessment_rules: The examination performance is taken in two individual examinations. The weighting is equal for both courses according to CP. The module grade MABB440A is calculated with equal weighting from the grades of MABB441A and MABB442A. Participation and active involvement in the exercises, as well as the successful completion of tasks, is a prerequisite for admission to the MABB442A examination.
bibliography: C.C. Rossow, K. Wolf, P. Horst, Handbuch der Luftfahrzeugtechnik, Hanser 2014
Bernard Etkin, Dynamics of Atmospheric Flight
Stephen Corda; Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
